profiles.ecg_smoke: Fast cache_sim smoke for the complete ECG policy set.
profiles.ecg_3sim_allalg_smoke: Bounded 3-simulator x 5-algorithm x 8-policy smoke matrix for final row/metric coverage.
profiles.ecg_3sim_realgraph_allalg: Three-simulator x three-real-graph x five-algorithm x eight-policy no-prefetch comparison.
profiles.ecg_3sim_realgraph_allalg_1b: Full-work cache_sim plus 1-billion-instruction detailed-ROI gem5/Sniper diagnostic on three real graphs.
profiles.ecg_3sim_sampled_allalg: Full-work three-simulator comparison on deterministic topology-derived samples of the three real graphs.
profiles.ecg_sniper_sampled_pr_streamengine: Equal-work sampled PageRank timing for GRASP, charged P-OPT, and ReusePlan-online+FlowThrough with fused Sniper record delivery.
profiles.ecg_sniper_realgraph_warm_probe: Full web-Google warm-SIFT LRU/ReusePlan probe with a 100-thousand-instruction detailed ROI.
profiles.ecg_sniper_realgraph_semantic_probe: Full web-Google warm-SIFT LRU/ReuseBind probe bounded at 100 thousand identical static edge visits.
profiles.ecg_sniper_realgraph_600m: Reference-compatible full-real-graph Sniper matrix with a detailed ROI capped at 600 million instructions.
profiles.ecg_sniper_semantic_gate: Five-kernel Sniper gate bounded by policy-independent static edge visits rather than committed instructions.
profiles.ecg_preliminary_5alg_3sim: Bounded five-algorithm, six-policy diagnostic matrix on a common synthetic graph across cache_sim, gem5, and Sniper.
profiles.ecg_preliminary_5alg_stride: Matched STRIDE8 sensitivity for the bounded five-algorithm, six-policy three-simulator diagnostic matrix.
profiles.ecg_gem5_hawkeye_gate: Five-algorithm gem5 real-instruction-PC Hawkeye comparison against the conventional baselines and ReusePlan.
profiles.ecg_replacement_baseline: Equal-capacity PR/BFS/SSSP/BC/CC replacement study with charged and uncharged P-OPT plus every static ReusePlan arm.
profiles.ecg_equal_capacity_16: Fresh full-graph 16-way ReusePlan counterpart for direct comparison against 14/15-way sensitivities.
profiles.ecg_equal_area_15: Full-graph 15-way ReusePlan sensitivity against 16-way baselines; intentionally undercharges the contextual metadata bit budget.
profiles.ecg_equal_area_14: Full-graph conservative integral equal-silicon sensitivity with 14-way ReusePlan against 16-way baselines.
profiles.ecg_online_dueling: Online ReusePlan set-dueling regret study against every static ReusePlan arm.
profiles.ecg_flowthrough_generality: Real-graph all-kernel comparison of always-allocate, static FlowThrough, and adaptive placement with the full baseline set.
profiles.ecg_cache_sim_factorial: Real-graph single-/two-epoch ReusePlan x FlowThrough cache_sim factorial with the full baseline set.
profiles.gem5_flowthrough_mechanism: Synthetic gem5 mechanism cell for fused ReusePlan versus ReusePlan+FlowThrough.
profiles.sniper_flowthrough_mechanism: Synthetic Sniper mechanism cell for fused ReusePlan versus ReusePlan+FlowThrough.
profiles.flowthrough_sniper_realgraph: Pending-calibration full-iteration web-Google PR Sniper matrix; do not freeze results with the rejected generic STRIDE8 configuration.
profiles.ecg_uniform_8mb_16: Uniform 8 MiB/16-way full-real-graph cache_sim matrix so every graph x kernel cell is directly comparable; supersedes the mixed 2 MiB/8 MiB factorial sizing.
profiles.ecg_uniform_8mb_16_stride8: Matched STRIDE8 twin of the uniform 8 MiB matrix. Every policy gets the same structure prefetcher, so demand-miss reduction (latency hiding) can be separated from total memory traffic (bandwidth), which prefetching cannot reduce.
profiles.ecg_record_width_timing: gem5 timing and bandwidth for the two-stamp record at the width gem5 actually streams; the width contrast itself lives in cache_sim.
profiles.ecg_isa_decode_matrix: Decode-cost matrix. Separates record WIDTH from the cost of DECODING it, with a per-stage LRU denominator so no comparison crosses runs.
profiles.ecg_fused_compact_matrix: Fused compact ReusePlan TimingSimple matrix: hardware-decoded 4B, software-widened 4B, and wide 8B controls in one build with per-stage LRU and ReusePlan-LRU; O3 request binding is a separate mechanism gate.
profiles.ecg_proposal_reuse_bind_o3_gate: Exact O3 request-bound correctness gate for the proposal's compact FlowThrough record load plus one-for-one computed-address ReuseBind property load.
profiles.reuse_plan_csr_transport_calibration: One complete cit-Patents-n18-sym i=1 O3 cell attributing the canonical-CSR ReusePlan transport path against its local LRU denominator.
profiles.reuse_plan_matched_policy_replay: One cit-Patents-n18-sym i=1 cache replay over transport-identical ReusePlan victim arms plus exact Belady.
profiles.reuse_plan_shortcircuit_timing: One cit-Patents-n18-sym i=1 O3 timing cell promoting the replay-selected shortcircuit arm against local LRU, transport control, and RRIP-first.
profiles.reuse_plan_epoch_attribution: One cit-Patents-n18-sym i=1 O3 cell measuring live ReusePlan stamp coverage and separating epoch, RRIP, and GRASP victim-rule contributions under identical compact FlowThrough transport.
profiles.reuse_plan_rrip_epoch_attribution: One cit-Patents-n18-sym i=1 O3 cell applying the metadata-disabled RRIP shadow as a real policy to isolate the end-to-end epoch contribution.
profiles.reuse_plan_rrip_recency_attribution: One cit-Patents-n18-sym i=1 O3 cell comparing RRIP epoch ranking against neutral property recency and positional controls.
profiles.reuse_plan_future_admission_screen: Three-graph cache_sim kill gate isolating request-bound future-distance admission from neutral recency eviction under symmetric FlowThrough.
profiles.reuse_plan_temporal_discrimination: Degree-identical PageRank controls that separate clustered from spread reader timing so GRASP sees the same degree signal and only the future mask changes.
profiles.reuse_plan_temporal_admission_gem5: Mechanism-only gem5 O3 validation of future-guided admission on the degree-controlled spread-reader graph.
profiles.reuse_plan_pagerank_study: Deterministic sampled PageRank study with static rrip_first+FlowThrough as the primary design.
profiles.reuse_plan_final_campaign: Stopped scale-limited pilot retained for auditability; not a publication campaign.
profiles.reuse_plan_literature_scale_campaign: Six-core literature-scale campaign with preordered graphs, sidecar-based gem5 timing, full-graph cache evidence, and bounded matched-work Sniper corroboration.
profiles.reuse_plan_twitter_scale_stress: Optional billion-edge Twitter-2010 cache-only stress profile.

reuse_plan_final_campaign.reason: The three-graph corpus is smaller than the GRASP/P-OPT evaluation scale. Use --list or --dry-run for audit only; publication requires the literature-scale replacement profile.

reuse_plan_literature_scale_campaign.reason: Run stages 60/90/91 first and require the literature-scale screen gate to pass before stages 92-95.

reuse_plan_twitter_scale_stress.reason: Twitter-2010 is optional and remains blocked until its converted graph receipt is complete.

stages.blocked_reason: The bounded matched-STRIDE diagnostic rejects Sniper's generic simple prefetcher; calibrate a traffic-bounded configuration before launching the full matrix.

stages.name: 31_gem5_record_width_4b
stages.notes: Compact 4-byte two-stamp record that substitutes for the CSR edge. Reports execution time, dram_offchip_bytes and dram_bus_util_pct. Expected behavior: with low DRAM utilization, reduced exposed misses should help both widths; with high utilization, the 8-byte arm should lose in proportion to traffic. Scope: gem5 PageRank only; the other kernels use 8-byte records. FlowThrough variants are excluded because their stream-load instruction is 8-byte only. ECG_EXPECT_BYTES_PER_EDGE aborts before the ROI on a width mismatch.

stages.name: 31_gem5_record_width_8b

Expected behavior: with low DRAM utilization, reduced exposed misses should help both widths; with high utilization, the 8-byte arm should lose in proportion to traffic. Scope: gem5 PageRank only; the other kernels use 8-byte records. FlowThrough variants are excluded because their stream-load instruction is 8-byte only. ECG_EXPECT_BYTES_PER_EDGE aborts before the ROI on a width mismatch.

stages.name: 40_isa_fused_4b
stages.notes: Fused ReuseBind-Indexed delivery, compact 4-byte record. Includes ECG:REUSE_PLAN_LRU so the replacement rule and the transport can be separated within the run. Every stage carries its OWN LRU cell so no ratio needs a denominator from another run: two nominally identical LRU cells were measured 1.74% apart in time purely because the guest's property arrays landed one page apart, which is the noise floor for cross-run ratios. Enforcement is live here (ECG_EXPECT_BYTES_PER_EDGE reaches the guest and aborts pre-ROI), unlike the earlier width matrix.

stages.name: 50_fused_compact_4b
stages.notes: Serialized single-core TimingSimple compact ReuseBind-Indexed arm; exact request binding is proven separately by the O3 mechanism probe. Runtime activation is attested by ECG_REUSE_BIND_ILOAD_C; the runner fails if the guest does not emit it. Every stage carries its own LRU and ReusePlan-LRU, and all stages use one build.

stages.name: 51_fused_software_4b
stages.notes: Matched serialized TimingSimple compact arm using the existing 64-bit fused ReuseBind-Indexed load after guest software widening. Decode control for stage 50.

stages.name: 52_fused_wide_8b
stages.notes: Matched serialized TimingSimple wide ReuseBind-Indexed arm. Implementation-width control for stage 50; every stage carries its own LRU and ReusePlan-LRU and all stages use one build.

stages.name: 60_gem5_proposal_reuse_bind_o3
stages.notes: Mechanism-only gate with a width-unmatched 8-byte non-FlowThrough ReusePlan semantic anchor plus transport-matched 4-byte FlowThrough lru_only and epoch_first arms. roi_matrix forces capped 2048-event ReuseBind and FlowThrough traces; every FlowThrough row must attest only 4-byte request-flag record loads, exact same-line O3 ReuseBind Request acceptance, and multiple nonzero record-derived plans. All three rows must match PageRank semantics. The anchor is not a FlowThrough control, and this proves existence and binding rather than request-count or performance coverage.

stages.name: 61_gem5_csr_transport_cit_i1
stages.notes: Single bounded transport calibration. Per-array x requestor LLC attribution must reconcile exactly before comparing the ReusePlan-LRU FlowThrough control with its same-job LRU denominator; no broader stage is unlocked by this run. Scope is single-core CPU data/instruction demand traffic with prefetching disabled. Unclassified-other CPU-data demand misses must remain at or below 2%. The graph is symmetrized, so incoming and outgoing CSR edge/index storage aliases; directed-graph attribution requires exporting the outgoing index range separately.

stages.name: 62_cache_sim_matched_policy_replay
stages.notes: Every ReusePlan arm uses identical 4-byte FlowThrough transport. T-OPT retains the common warm prefix to establish cache state, marks the cache-stat reset as ROI start, fingerprints only ROI requests, and counts oracle hits/misses only in the ROI suffix; next-use optimization still sees the full warm+ROI sequence. The runner requires the exact six-arm ReusePlan roster to produce one identical post-L2 address/class/read-write fingerprint and Belady result, checks ROI trace accesses equal measured LLC accesses, and requires the oracle floor not exceed measured misses before comparing victim rules. LRU and native GRASP are reference rows with explicitly independent oracle-group hashes.

stages.name: 63_gem5_shortcircuit_cit_i1
stages.notes: Single replay-promoted timing cell. The 4-byte compact record is fail-closed, per-array attribution must validate, FlowThrough records must cold-miss exactly once per line, and all comparisons use one local LRU denominator. This is one n18 sample point, not a general performance claim.

stages.name: 64_gem5_epoch_attribution_cit_i1
stages.notes: Decisive epoch-efficacy cell. All ReusePlan arms use identical 4-byte compact FlowThrough transport. Resettable replacement-policy counters quantify request validity, live stamped ways, context mismatches, zero-stamped selections, stamped victims selected through an epoch-capable path, epoch-decisive selections from a metadata-disabled shadow decision, and victim-way concentration. Eligibility is a liveness check; only the decisive counter shows that epoch metadata changed a victim. Compare RRIP-first against GRASP-only for the combined RRIP path, and epoch-first against the records-first/property-LRU arm for an exact runtime epoch contrast. Do not infer a future-reference benefit from RRIP behavior alone.

stages.name: 65_gem5_rrip_epoch_attribution_cit_i1
stages.notes: Applied positional counterfactual. RRIP-no-epoch keeps the exact RRIP eligibility gate, records-first selection, insertion, transport, and guest work of RRIP-first while replacing epoch distance with fixed set order. This stage measures epoch-path versus positional selection; stage 66 supplies the neutral property-recency epoch-information test. GRASP-only and transport-LRU remain local decomposition controls.

stages.name: 66_gem5_rrip_recency_attribution_cit_i1
stages.notes: Neutral epoch-information test. All three ReusePlan arms share RRIP eligibility, aging, records-first selection, insertion, compact transport, and guest work. The positional control chooses the first property candidate; the neutral control chooses the oldest property candidate; RRIP-first uses epoch distance. Epoch information is useful only if RRIP-first materially beats the recency control.

stages.name: 67_cache_sim_future_admission_i1
stages.notes: Signal gate, not a novelty claim. The recency-admission treatment and recency control differ only in future-distance admission/refresh. The future-tier arm tests the intended combined mask at eviction: future distance first, carried GRASP tier on epoch ties, then recency. The admission+epoch arm completes the admission x eviction interaction. All ReusePlan arms share compact records and FlowThrough; LRU and GRASP receive the same generic structural FlowThrough opportunity. scripts/experiments/ecg/analysis/future_admission_gate.py compares each treatment to its named matched control using the unweighted geometric mean of per-graph ratios. Promote to gem5 only if a treatment reaches at most 0.97 for both LLC misses and total off-chip traffic, with neither metric above 1.02 on any graph. P-OPT/Hawkeye comparison remains mandatory before any novelty claim.

stages.name: 68_cache_sim_temporal_discrimination_i1
stages.notes: Mechanism discrimination, not a performance claim. Both symmetrized graphs derive from 65,536-vertex, degree-eight directed inputs and have identical serialized counts and degree sequences. Clustered readers are adjacent in the preserved vertex sweep; spread readers are separated across the graph. GRASP receives the same degree distribution in both cells. This stage isolates eviction ranking; admission is evaluated on the real-graph stage because clustered reuse is absorbed by private caches and produces no LLC admission updates. A future-mask policy must respond to the timing change while preserving exact semantics and symmetric FlowThrough.

stages.name: 69_gem5_temporal_admission_i1
stages.notes: Mechanism-only matched O3 test on the directed spread-reader graph. Both rows use the corrected builder-v2 mask, compact 4-byte FlowThrough records, request-bound ReuseBind, RRIP eligibility/aging, and property-recency eviction. Only future-distance admission/refresh changes. Array-attribution schema 2 separately accounts incoming traversal and outgoing-degree CSR offsets. One architectural record sweep is required; O3 replay may add at most 0.5% record-line misses, while a second sweep remains fail-closed. This synthetic control cannot support a general performance or novelty claim.
